title: Your own voice
job: An eight-sentence piece that changes register midway
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: REGISTER CHANGES WHEN THE ADDRESSEE CHANGES, NOT WHEN THE MOOD DOES. A speaker does not slide into -(seu)pnida because the subject turned serious. They change because they have turned to a room, stepped up to a counter, or begun to speak on the record.
SO THE TRIGGER HAS TO BE VISIBLE IN THE PIECE: a new addressee named, a threshold crossed, a quotation begun. A piece that changes ending with nothing to change it for is this module's failure mode.

THIS COURSE HAS EXACTLY TWO SPEECH LEVELS AND HERE THAT IS A FEATURE: plain -yo and L4-M7's deferential -(seu)pnida. Three shapes work — an account that ends formally, one that quotes an announcement, and one that begins formally and drops to -yo.

-GESSEUMNIDA COMMITS. hagesseumnida is I will do it, deurigesseumnida is I will do it for you, and both are what a speaker says at the moment they take the floor. They are the only two surfaces this module adds.

THE OTHER AXES MOVE WITH IT. L3-M8's honorific -si- on the person spoken about, the formal chip, and L2-M2's address terms — together they make a switch read as a change of stance rather than of grammar.

THE WHOLE LEVEL MAY APPEAR: M1's idiom, at most one and only in the -yo half; M2's disclaimer; M3's -neyo and -jyo; M4's formula; M5's nominalised clause; M6's discourse frame; M7's hint; M8's repair; M9's frame narrator.

AND SOME THINGS STILL MAY NOT: no dialect production, no new abstract noun, no written -(neu)nda, and no banmal — including inside a quotation, which is where a flustered narrator reaches for it first.
EIGHT SENTENCES IS A CEILING, NOT A TARGET. This is the last rung of the product and its exit is assembly rather than acquisition, so the spend is two surfaces and everything else is reused.

sentences.cue: A friend got married today. It was lovely. And I gave the toast. Everyone, thank you sincerely. I will raise a glass to my friend.

words.note: The deferential I will: -gesseumnida on a verb stem. It is what a speaker says at the moment they take the floor, which is why it marks the switch rather than following it.

sentences.trap: English would carry the shift in words — a warmer vocabulary for the room. Korean carries it in the ending alone, and yeoreobun is what tells the listener the ending is about to change.

mistake.display: Oneul chingu-ga gyeolhon-eul hasyeotseumnida. Jeongmal joasseumnida.
mistake.script: 오늘 친구가 결혼을 하셨습니다. 정말 좋았습니다.
mistake.why: The whole account has gone deferential because the day was important. Nothing has changed about who is being spoken to, so nothing should have changed about the ending.

sentences.usage: Telling a friend about a day, and then standing up at it.
sentences.mnemonic: yeoreobun is the doorway; the ending changes as you go through it.

sentences.cue: I was working at the station yesterday. A lot of people came. So I made an announcement. Everyone, here is an announcement: the train departs shortly. Now I am home. I am tired.

words.cue: I will do it for you (deferential)
words.note: hagesseumnida done for somebody else: deurida is the humble give, so this is I will do it for you. malsseum deurigesseumnida opens almost every formal address.

sentences.trap: The quoted announcement is deferential and the sentences around it are not, and that is correct. A quotation carries its own footing, so the register inside the marks says nothing about the register outside them.

mistake.display: Geuraeseo bangsong-eul haesseumnida. Yeoreobun, annae malsseum deurigesseumnida.
mistake.script: 그래서 방송을 했습니다. 여러분, 안내 말씀 드리겠습니다.
mistake.why: The narration has been dragged up to the level of the thing being narrated. You are telling a friend about your shift; only the words inside the quotation marks were said to a station.

sentences.usage: Telling somebody what you had to announce at work.
sentences.mnemonic: The quotation keeps its own level; you keep yours.

sentences.display: Oneul hoesa-eseo hoeui-ga isseoyo. Jeo-neun jom bappeundeyo. Sajangnim-kkeseo "Jigeum sijakhapsida" rago malsseumhasyeosseoyo. Yeoreobun, je-ga bogoseo-reul malsseum deurigesseumnida.

words.cue: I will do it for you (deferential)

sentences.trap: L4-M5's trailing -neundeyo in the second sentence is a hedge to a friend, and it could not survive the switch. Once you are addressing the room the hedging goes and the ending carries the politeness instead.

variations.cue: Everyone, I will present the report.
variations.changed: the formal half alone: standing up

mistake.why: The hedge has been carried through the switch. -neundeyo softens between equals; in front of a room it undercuts the very footing the deferential ending just claimed.

sentences.usage: Standing up in a meeting you have been dreading.
sentences.mnemonic: Hedge to a friend, commit to a room.

sentences.mnemonic: The room arrives, the level rises; the room leaves, it falls.

sentences.cue: I studied at school today. It was really hard. Even so, it was good. The class ended. And then a lot of people came. Everyone, thank you very much. I will do my best.
sentences.literal: today school-at studied. really was-hard. even-so was-interesting. class-SUBJ ended. and people-SUBJ many came. everyone, really thank-DEF. well will-do-DEF

words.note: The deferential I will: -gesseumnida on a verb stem. It is what a speaker says at the moment they take the floor, which is why it marks the switch rather than following it.

sentences.trap: Seven sentences and one new word between them. The last rung of this course is assembly: everything here was bought on a rung below, and the only thing being learnt is when the ending moves.

mistake.display: Oneul hakgyo-eseo gongbuhaesseoyo. Jal hagesseumnida. Jeongmal himdeureosseoyo.
mistake.script: 오늘 학교에서 공부했어요. 잘 하겠습니다. 정말 힘들었어요.
mistake.why: The level rose for one sentence and fell again with nobody addressed on either side. A switch with no trigger is the failure mode of this module, and it reads as a slip rather than as a move.

sentences.usage: Closing an account by turning to the people in it.
sentences.mnemonic: Assemble what you have; move the ending once, on purpose.

comprehensionPool.cue: I will raise a glass to my friend.
I am a bit busy, though.
Everyone, I will do my best.
Now I work at a school.
May the departed rest in peace.
Once upon a time an old woman lived in the countryside.
Now a friend has come. The mood is good.
